title: Small firms struggle with slow-paying customers and manual payment handling

history.reason: Federal Reserve payments report read directly; evidence articulates the issue but not its cost.

description: Many small employer firms that bill after delivery report that customers pay slowly, and some report time-consuming billing and deposit processes and settlement delays.
customer_segment: US small employer firms (1-499 employees) that collect payment after delivery, on a schedule, in installments or via third parties; professional services/real estate and manufacturing are more often in this group.
context: Self-reported challenges from an opt-in module of the 2023 Small Business Credit Survey (Federal Reserve Banks).

evidence.text: 39% of surveyed employer firms said customers are slow to pay; 20% cited time-consuming processes such as billing and bank deposits; 18% cited settlement delays (N=4,858).
Slow-paying customers are more commonly reported by firms collecting payment after delivery, on a schedule, in installments, or through a third party.
Late payment is common but its dollar and time cost to firms is not measured in this source.
Some firms may value invoicing and collections automation enough to pay for it.

alternatives: Accounting and invoicing software, factoring, and payment-processing services: not yet investigated.

contradictory_evidence.text: Fees (52%) were the most common payments challenge; slow payment (39%) and time-consuming processes (20%) were less common, and 20% of firms reported no payments challenges.
Reporting a challenge does not show it is costly enough to justify a purchase; the survey does not measure cost, time spent or willingness to pay.

uncertainty: Unknown: severity (days late, dollars outstanding), which industries and sizes are most affected, existing tool adoption, and willingness to pay. The segment definition is broad.
open_questions: How late and how large are the receivables, by industry and firm size?
Which firms already use invoicing/collections tools and what gaps remain?
Is the problem different for very small firms (excluded as non-employer here)?
next_actions: Find independent data on days-sales-outstanding and late-payment costs for small firms (e.g., Census, Federal Reserve, SBA sources).
Review public documentation of existing invoicing and collections products.
